notable_qa.question: Despite a healthy TCV, why did management narrow the guidance band, and what opportunities and challenges does Infosys see in securing enterprise systems against AI-driven cyber attacks?
notable_qa.answer: Management explained that guidance reflects strong AI growth and mega deals, offset by AI productivity impacts, competitive intensity, changing offshore ratios, and selective contract choices based on economic thresholds.
supporting_quotes: Despite a healthy TCV, why did you sort of narrow the guidance band?

notable_qa.question: What changed most in the growth guidance revision versus last quarter, and what are the largest drivers?
notable_qa.answer: Management cited pricing pressure from competitive intensity, softer than expected volume growth, and slower discretionary spend in Retail and Hi-Tech sectors.
supporting_quotes: If you look at what we are seeing today is a pricing pressure on the back of competitive intensity, which has increased in the last couple of quarters.

We saw softer than expected revenue growth or a volume growth in the quarter. So that was the second reason. And slower discretionary spend in some of the sectors, especially the Retail and HiTech that we called out.

risks.risk: Softer Q2 volumes, competitive intensity, and pricing pressure leading to downward guidance revision.
risks.speaker: Jayesh Sanghrajka
risks.quote: Our Q2 has been softer and our volume continues to remain softer. We have also seen pricing pressure on the back of competitive intensity and higher ask on productivity.

risks.risk: Discretionary spending softness in Retail and Hi-Tech sectors.
risks.speaker: Jayesh Sanghrajka
risks.quote: On top of that, as Salil said, some of the sectors, we see softness, Retail, Hi-Tech, where the discretionary is lower than what we are expecting.

risks.risk: Expected margin headwinds in the second half from compensation hikes and continued pricing intensity.
risks.speaker: Jayesh Sanghrajka
risks.quote: As you look forward, the next half, which is H2, we will have impact coming from compensation, as you rightly said, so that will have a headwind. We will see continued intensity on pricing.

strategic_commitments.claim: Capital allocation policy aims to return 85% of free cash flow back to shareholders over a five-year period through a combination of dividend and buyback.
strategic_commitments.speaker: Jayesh Sanghrajka
strategic_commitments.quote: So, I think if you look at our capital allocation policy that we rolled out almost two years back, we had very clearly said that 85% of the free cash flow that we generate, we will return back to shareholders over a five-year period.
